Methods for elementfit objects

Source: R/element.R
elementfit_methods.Rd

Methods for element fits from fit_element. The predictor is proportional mass remaining, so newdata gives mass remaining values.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'elementfit'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'elementfit'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'elementfit'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'elementfit'
residuals(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'elementfit'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'elementfit'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'elementfit'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'elementfit'
tidy(x, boot = NULL, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'elementfit'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'elementfit'
augment(x, newdata = NULL, boot = NULL, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

x, object

an elementfit object

...

unused

newdata

optional numeric vector of mass remaining values, or (for augment()) a data frame with a mass column

boot

optional litfit_bootstrap object from bootstrap_parameters for the same fit

conf.level

confidence level for intervals and bands

Value

tidy(), glance() and augment() return a data.frame (see litfit_tidiers for the shared columns; augment() uses mass and element columns). plot() and print() return x invisibly.

Details

glance() reports, besides information criteria, the peak proportional element remaining (peak_element) and the mass remaining at which it occurs (mass_at_peak). A peak of 1 at a mass of 1 means no net immobilisation.

Examples

fit <- fit_element(
  mass.remaining = pineneedles$Mass.remaining,
  element.remaining = c(1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1, 0.8, 0.6),
  iters = 200, quiet = TRUE
)
coef(fit)
#>         a         b 
#> 0.4919647 0.6456967 
predict(fit, newdata = c(1, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25))
#> [1] 1.0000000 1.2980816 1.2015235 0.5550716
tidy(fit)
#>   term  estimate
#> 1    a 0.4919647
#> 2    b 0.6456967
glance(fit)
#>          model nobs nparams      sigma   logLik       AIC      AICc       BIC
#> 1 import.model    6       2 0.06808585 7.608284 -11.21657 -7.216568 -11.63305
#>   converged peak_element mass_at_peak
#> 1      TRUE     1.357312    0.6456784
head(augment(fit, newdata = seq(1, 0, by = -0.1)))
#>   mass  .fitted
#> 1  1.0 1.000000
#> 2  0.9 1.118508
#> 3  0.8 1.242870
#> 4  0.7 1.339351
#> 5  0.6 1.342427
#> 6  0.5 1.201523
